claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and any children you're responsible for.

Let me start with a few basic questions:

**How many children are you responsible for, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi there! I'm looking into whether I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I have one child to assess - Alex.

To help me determine your eligibility, I need to gather some details about Alex's situation.

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 14, they're under 16, which is good for Child Benefit eligibility.

Now I need to understand your living situation with Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or does Alex live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, that's helpful to know. Now I need to understand your residency status to determine your eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't - I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Living abroad does affect Child Benefit eligibility, but there are some circumstances where you may still be able to claim.

**Can you tell me what your current employment or residency status is abroad? For example, are you a Crown servant, or do you have any specific status that might allow you to claim Child Benefit while living outside the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't have any special status like that. I'm just living abroad as a regular resident.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility.

Let me explain the situation: According to the Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you **live in the UK**. There are exceptions for certain circumstances, such as if you're a Crown servant or if you move to the UK and have the right to reside, but these don't apply to your situation.

Since you're living abroad as a regular resident without any special status that would allow you to claim Child Benefit from outside the UK, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: If your circumstances change in the future—for example, if you move back to the UK—you would be able to reconsider your eligibility for Child Benefit at that time. Is there anything else I can help you with?
